source_tools.relevance: All sequence properties, domains, homology, and annotation evidence

entities.name: RibBA
observations: Reviewed RibBA proteins catalyze both 3,4-dihydroxy-2-butanone 4-phosphate synthase activity and GTP cyclohydrolase II activity.
RibBA participates in two early branches/steps of bacterial riboflavin biosynthesis.
Reported metal requirements are two Mg2+ or Mn2+ ions and one Zn2+ ion per subunit.
Associated EC numbers are 4.1.99.12 and 3.5.4.25; associated Rhea reactions are RHEA:18457 and RHEA:23704.
Homolog annotations include cytosolic localization and GO terms for riboflavin biosynthesis, metal ion binding, DHBP synthase, and GTP cyclohydrolase II.

source_tools.relevance: Reviewed homolog functional, cofactor, pathway, reaction, and GO annotations

entities.name: Riboflavin biosynthesis
observations: The candidate is strongly inferred to catalyze the first DHBP-synthase reaction from D-ribulose 5-phosphate and the first GTP-cyclohydrolase-II reaction in the riboflavin pathway.
The two reactions produce intermediates that feed downstream flavin mononucleotide and flavin adenine dinucleotide biosynthesis.

source_tools.relevance: Pathway assignment from reviewed RibBA homologs

entities.name: RHEA:18457
observations: D-ribulose 5-phosphate is converted to (2S)-2-hydroxy-3-oxobutyl phosphate and formate by the DHBP synthase module.
The corresponding EC annotation in reviewed RibBA homologs is EC 4.1.99.12.

entities.name: RHEA:23704
observations: GTP is converted to a hydroxylated pyrimidine ribonucleotide intermediate with formate and phosphate products by the GTP cyclohydrolase II module.
The corresponding EC annotation in reviewed RibBA homologs is EC 3.5.4.25.
